key_insight: Joint multilingual training delivered the strongest cardiology entity recognition in nearly all settings, while specialty-specific pretraining had limited downstream impact.
clinical_relevance: CardioLM could support extraction of diseases, symptoms, procedures, and medications from multilingual cardiology text, but clinical workflow benefits remain unproven.
method: Built CardioCCC from 508 Spanish cardiology case reports, extended to six other languages through translation, annotation projection, and clinician review.
Continued cardiology and biomedical pretraining to create language-specific CardioBERTa encoders.
Fine-tuned CardioNER models and compared monolingual systems with jointly trained multilingual models.
evidence_signal: Multilingual models exceeded the strongest monolingual system by up to 0.13 strict F1; clinicians’ mean ratings rose from 26% for a rule-and-dictionary baseline to 73% for CardioNER.
watch_item: Performance on translated case reports may not generalize to native-language clinical records, and entity-boundary errors remain substantial.
paper_title: CardioLM: A multilingual suite of small language models for the cardiology domain
